# T02 — Durable jobs and launch controls
Research: TinyFish search/fetch, 2026-11-01. No browser/visual testing.

- [SQLite RETURNING](https://sqlite.org/lang_returning.html): UPDATE…RETURNING claims and returns the updated row; commit the transaction before exposing it. BEGIN IMMEDIATE plus a running-CFD exclusion keeps concurrent claimers from double claiming or crossing the CFD resource lock.
- [FastAPI background tasks](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/background-tasks/): heavy work should not be tied to the request process. API endpoints only enqueue; a separate local worker executes allowlisted subprocesses.
- [shadcn Sheet](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/sheet): right-side complementary detail with dialog semantics, keyboard focus and close controls. The CLI prompted for a new component library despite --yes, so small local wrappers use the already installed Radix Dialog primitive, matching the existing house component style. No dependency added.
- Installed stack verified in package.json and pyproject.toml: SQLite stdlib, FastAPI/Pydantic 2, Radix UI 1.8.1, React 19.3, TanStack Query 5.105.0, Zod 4.6.7.

## Visual references
- https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/sheet — preserve the narrow right-side detail drawer, title/description hierarchy and explicit dismissal. The fetched page exposed no image URLs; no product-image assets are embedded.

## Decisions
- Two subprocess slots permit numerical/import work alongside one CFD-family operation. cfd_viz shares that lock to avoid simultaneous solver/postprocessing pressure.
- CFD ranks are capped at min(requested, 8, max(1, cpu_count−2)). Existing output IDs are refused and reserved across queued jobs.
- Numerical job completion does not imply accepted CFD. Rejected scientific results retain their existing acceptance data.
- For this resource-constrained Mac, queue jobs in the UI and run the worker after closing dev servers/browser. No worker starts automatically with the API.
